evidence.note: Six upfront TaskCreate calls form a dependency-ordered pipeline plan (lexer→preprocessor→parser→sema→codegen→iterate), with foundational representation work (symbol tables, type resolution, struct layout in task 40) sequenced before dependent codegen (task 41). This is genuine dependency-aware staging, exceeding a mere mental list.
Tasks are marked in_progress/completed as each stage is finished, showing an actively tracked staged plan across the horizon rather than abandoned early planning.
Gets simplest programs (return 42, then printf) compiling before running the full 780-test suite — the 'simplest first, then layer features' pattern of anchor 5.

The bulk of the work is reactive: run suite, list failures, pick one feature (bitfields, complex, vectors, compound literals, nested funcs, stkalign), fix, re-run. No pre-named feature milestones with designated certifying tests; the done-signal is ad-hoc failing tests and eventual full-suite 100%, short of an explicit maintained milestone hierarchy.

reasoning: The agent built an explicit, dependency-ordered stage plan up front that correctly puts representation (types/symbol tables) before codegen and drives simplest-programs-first, which lands above anchor 5. But the milestones are coarse pipeline components rather than language-feature milestones each naming its certifying tests, and the long tail of work is reactive test-failure-chasing rather than a re-ordered, per-milestone-certified hierarchy, so it does not reach anchor 8. This places the observed behavior at a 6.
